# mewkit CLI reference

Every command the CLI declares, with its subcommands and flags, as clap prints them.
Generated from the command definition, so a verb named here exists and a verb missing
here does not.

Exit codes: `0` ran and succeeded · `1` ran and failed · `2` the invocation was wrong
(unknown command, unknown subcommand, or a missing subcommand on a command that requires
one). `mewkit <command> <subcommand> --help` prints that subcommand's usage and runs nothing.

## mewkit init

```text
Install the kit into this project, or your home with --global

Usage: mewkit init [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --target <TARGETS>      Runtimes to install for: claude-code, codex, cursor (comma-separated) or all. Omitted: Claude Code with --yes or in a project that has `.claude/`, otherwise a picker
      --profile <PROFILE>     Claude Code: install a subset (core, developer, product, atlassian, security, research, or full). Re-running with a narrower profile removes what the narrower profile no longer includes, unless you edited it
      --skill-packs <PACKS>   Codex and Cursor: comma-separated skill packs, or `all`. Omitted installs every skill; an empty value installs the default pack only
      --delivery <SHAPE>      Claude Code only: `native` (the host's own directory) or `plugin` (the same content plus a plugin manifest)
      --mcp-profiles <NAMES>  Cursor: MCP profile names, or `all`, to merge into .cursor/mcp.json. Without it no MCP config is written
      --allow-cloud-mcp       Cursor: second opt-in for applying an MCP profile to a project that has a git remote (Cursor Cloud Agents run no local MCP hooks)
      --allow-kit-source      Run even in the MeowKit source repo (whose `.claude/` is the kit's authored source, and which an install would overwrite)
      --dry-run               Show what would change and change nothing installed (a downloaded kit is still kept in the cache)
  -y, --yes                   Answer every question with its default and do not ask any
      --global                Act on your home directory instead of this project
      --json                  Print one JSON document instead of text
      --force                 Replace or remove files you edited after the kit installed them
      --kit-version <TAG>     Install exactly this kit release (e.g. v2.16.0)
      --beta                  Let a prerelease be the newest kit
      --offline               Make no network request: use the newest kit in this scope's cache (or the cached --kit-version)
      --kit-archive <ZIP>     Install from a local meowkit-release.zip; its SHA-256 comes from --kit-sha256 or a checksums.txt beside it
      --kit-sha256 <HEX>      
      --allow-unverified-kit  Accept a kit with no checksum or no kit-contract.json
  -h, --help                  Print help
```

## mewkit upgrade

```text
Move the installed runtimes to a newer kit, keeping your edits

Usage: mewkit upgrade [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --target <TARGETS>      Only these installed runtimes (comma-separated); default: every one here
      --dry-run               Show what would change and change nothing installed (a downloaded kit is still kept in the cache)
      --check                 Report the installed kit against the newest release; change nothing
      --list                  List the kit releases that can be installed; change nothing
      --no-cleanup            Accepted for scripts written for the npm CLI. There is no download directory to keep: a downloaded kit always stays in the cache
      --yes                   Confirm --force in a session with no terminal (CI, a pipe, a hook)
      --global                Act on your home directory instead of this project
      --json                  Print one JSON document instead of text
      --force                 Replace or remove files you edited after the kit installed them
      --kit-version <TAG>     Install exactly this kit release (e.g. v2.16.0)
      --beta                  Let a prerelease be the newest kit
      --offline               Make no network request: use the newest kit in this scope's cache (or the cached --kit-version)
      --kit-archive <ZIP>     Install from a local meowkit-release.zip; its SHA-256 comes from --kit-sha256 or a checksums.txt beside it
      --kit-sha256 <HEX>      
      --allow-unverified-kit  Accept a kit with no checksum or no kit-contract.json
  -h, --help                  Print help
```

## mewkit doctor

```text
Check the toolchain, the installs here and their hooks

Usage: mewkit doctor [OPTIONS] [SUBCOMMAND]

Arguments:
  [SUBCOMMAND]  `provenance`: what the install baseline can and cannot prove

Options:
      --report            Append a shareable report block to the text output
      --providers         Also report what each provider adapter can enforce
      --state             Also report the state taxonomy
      --explain           `provenance`: name the files behind each count
      --hard-gates        Live-probe the hard gates (plan, privacy, injection, ship) in a scratch project
      --adopt             Rebuild the npm CLI's ownership baseline from the local kit cache, or refuse
      --target <TARGETS>  Only these runtimes (comma-separated); default: all
      --global            Check your home directory's installs first instead of this project's
      --json              Print one JSON document instead of text
  -h, --help              Print help
```

## mewkit self-update

```text
Replace this binary with the newest release (SHA-256 verified)

Usage: mewkit self-update [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --check              Only report whether a newer binary exists (exit 3 when one does)
      --channel <CHANNEL>  Release channel: stable, or beta to include prereleases [default: stable] [possible values: stable, beta]
  -h, --help               Print help
```

## mewkit orient

```text
Resume orientation from durable task state; reads records only

Usage: mewkit orient [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --json       Print the full envelope as JSON instead of the bounded text block
      --record     Record the advisory `orient_run` measurement (the default)
      --no-record  Skip the advisory measurement, leaving the run strictly read-only
  -h, --help       Print help
```

## mewkit plan

```text
Inspect, approve or archive a plan under tasks/plans/

Usage: mewkit plan <COMMAND>

Commands:
  status   Progress across plan.md + its phase files (read-only)
  check    Required-section report for one phase file (read-only)
  approve  Stamp the Gate 1 approval receipt (mutating)
  archive  Mark statuses completed + move to tasks/plans/archive/ (mutating)
  help     Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help
```

### mewkit plan status

```text
Progress across plan.md + its phase files (read-only)

Usage: mewkit plan status [OPTIONS] [TARGET]

Arguments:
  [TARGET]  The plan directory

Options:
      --json  Print the summary as JSON instead of the progress block
  -h, --help  Print help
```

### mewkit plan check

```text
Required-section report for one phase file (read-only)

Usage: mewkit plan check [OPTIONS] [TARGET]

Arguments:
  [TARGET]  The phase file, or the plan.md / plan directory with --structural

Options:
      --json        
      --structural  Validate plan.md + every sibling phase file against the full template
  -h, --help        Print help
```

### mewkit plan approve

```text
Stamp the Gate 1 approval receipt (mutating)

Usage: mewkit plan approve [OPTIONS] [TARGET]

Arguments:
  [TARGET]  The plan directory, or a plan.md inside it

Options:
      --by <BY>      Approver name recorded on the approval receipt
      --activate     Also activate the task durably; the npm CLI's default is OFF
      --no-activate  The explicit opt-out, accepted so a caller can state the default
  -h, --help         Print help
```

### mewkit plan archive

```text
Mark statuses completed + move to tasks/plans/archive/ (mutating)

Usage: mewkit plan archive [OPTIONS] [TARGET]

Arguments:
  [TARGET]  The plan directory, or a plan.md inside it

Options:
      --dry-run  Print what would happen without writing or moving anything
  -h, --help     Print help
```

## mewkit task

```text
Create and list task files

Usage: mewkit task <COMMAND>

Commands:
  new   Scaffold a task file from the template for its type
  list  List task files with their status, type, priority and path
  help  Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help
```

### mewkit task new

```text
Scaffold a task file from the template for its type

Usage: mewkit task new [OPTIONS] [DESCRIPTION]...

Arguments:
  [DESCRIPTION]...  The description, also the source of the slug and the title. Taken as every remaining positional joined by a space, so a description that escaped its quotes still reads as one sentence

Options:
      --type <TYPE>          Task type: feature, bug-fix, refactor, security
      --priority <PRIORITY>  Task priority
      --activate             Activate the task on creation; `--no-activate` opts out
      --no-activate          
  -h, --help                 Print help
```

### mewkit task list

```text
List task files with their status, type, priority and path

Usage: mewkit task list [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --all              Include completed and backlog tasks (scan all of `tasks/`)
      --status <STATUS>  Filter the list by status: draft, in-progress, blocked, review, done
  -h, --help             Print help
```

## mewkit task-state

```text
Show or update the durable task record

Usage: mewkit task-state [OPTIONS] [COMMAND]

Commands:
  show    Print the durable state every active record carries
  update  Record a transition on one task's record
  help    Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --json  Emit machine-readable JSON (`show` only)
  -h, --help  Print help
```

### mewkit task-state show

```text
Print the durable state every active record carries

Usage: mewkit task-state show [OPTIONS] [TASK-ID]

Arguments:
  [TASK-ID]  Accepted and ignored: the pointer, not an argument, decides which record is the current one

Options:
      --json  Emit machine-readable JSON (`show` only)
  -h, --help  Print help
```

### mewkit task-state update

```text
Record a transition on one task's record

Usage: mewkit task-state update [OPTIONS] [TASK-ID]

Arguments:
  [TASK-ID]  The task whose record to update

Options:
      --status <STATUS>                 Task status: active, blocked, done
      --step <STEP>                     What just finished
      --json                            Emit machine-readable JSON (`show` only)
      --next <NEXT>                     The next action
      --plan <PLAN>                     Path to the plan this record joins
      --blocker <TEXT>                  Record a blocker; repeatable
      --verification <REF=RESULT>       Record a verification as `ref=result`; repeatable
      --evidence-ref <PATH>             Record an evidence reference; repeatable
      --capability-decision <DECISION>  Record a capability decision as `capId|decision|reason`; repeatable
  -h, --help                            Print help
```

## mewkit validate

```text
Check this project's structure and wiring (not that the gates block)

Usage: mewkit validate [OPTIONS] [DIR]

Arguments:
  [DIR]  The generated target directory to validate (with `--target`)

Options:
      --mode <MODE>        Maintainer override for the detected consumer profile
      --target <PROVIDER>  Validate a generated provider target instead of a `.claude/` project
      --portable           Include the portable provider-contract checks
      --strict             Treat WARN as failure (exit 1)
      --workflow           Run only the workflow.yaml drift check
      --gates              Run only the gate-authority contract check
      --ownership          Run only the artifact ownership-completeness check
      --agents             Run only the declared agent-contract conformance checks
      --substrate          Run only the responsibility-substrate drift and untagged check
      --packs              Run only the pack-manifest coherence and safety check
      --rules              Run only the routing-table-breadth check
      --capabilities       Run only the capability-manifest checks
      --memory             Run only the committed team-memory store lint
      --frontmatter        Run only the SKILL.md frontmatter schema and runtime-contract check
      --docs-refs          Run only the `.claude` to `docs/*` reference allowlist check
  -h, --help               Print help
```

## mewkit review

```text
Prepare, read, compose and submit a structured code review

Usage: mewkit review [OPTIONS] [SUBCOMMAND] [TARGET]

Arguments:
  [SUBCOMMAND]  `prepare`, `read`, `coverage`, `compose`, `submit` or `cleanup`
  [TARGET]      `prepare`: the PR URL, `owner/repo#n` or number. `read`: the path

Options:
      --remote <REMOTE>    `prepare`: fetch the pull request from this remote
      --session <SESSION>  The session id `review prepare` printed
      --as <REVIEWER>      `read`: the reviewer role the receipt is attributed to
      --reply              `submit`: the only GitHub write authority
      --confirm <CONFIRM>  `submit`: the token bound to the composed payload
      --json               Print JSON instead of a summary line
  -h, --help               Print help
```

## mewkit advice

```text
Athena supervision checkpoints: evidence in, advice out (never approval)

Usage: mewkit advice [OPTIONS] [SUBCOMMAND]

Arguments:
  [SUBCOMMAND]  `begin`, `commit`, `status` or `validate-packet`

Options:
      --run <RUN>
          The supervision run id; it names the dossier
      --skill <SKILL>
          The wrapped skill, e.g. `mk:cook`
      --stage <STAGE>
          GUIDE, RESCUE, REVIEW or RECHECK
      --checkpoint <CHECKPOINT>
          Caller-chosen checkpoint id, unique within the run
      --disposition <DISPOSITION>
          The returned routing signal, recorded verbatim
      --outcome <OUTCOME>
          What the PARENT did with the directive: adopted, rejected, deferred
      --reason <REASON>
          Why — required even when the directive was adopted
      --question <QUESTION>
          The question the checkpoint asked
      --directive <DIRECTIVE>
          The directive that came back
      --correction <CORRECTION>
          One required correction; repeat for more
      --evidence-pointer <EVIDENCE_POINTER>
          One evidence pointer; repeat for more
      --next <NEXT>
          The next safe action recorded on the receipt
      --slug <SLUG>
          Receipt filename slug; defaults to the run id
      --task-id <TASK_ID>
          Task id recorded on the receipt
      --provider <PROVIDER>
          Runtime recorded on the receipt
      --evidence <EVIDENCE>
          `commit`: the workflow evidence index a correction supersedes. `validate-packet`: the packet to check
      --correction-kind <CORRECTION_KIND>
          `commit`: source or scope — scope also returns Gate 1 to required
      --packet-kind <PACKET_KIND>
          `validate-packet`: input, output or brief
      --release-stage <RELEASE_STAGE>
          The release stage whose budget this call spends (`mk:ship` only)
      --json
          `status`: print the dossier as JSON
  -h, --help
          Print help
```

## mewkit trace

```text
On-demand trace recall: score, audit, propose, record friction

Usage: mewkit trace [OPTIONS] [SUBCOMMAND]

Arguments:
  [SUBCOMMAND]  `score`, `audit` or `propose`; none prints the usage

Options:
      --id <ID>                          Run id: filters `score`, attributes `--friction`
      --friction <FRICTION>              Record a friction note instead of reading the log
      --responsibility <RESPONSIBILITY>  Attribute the friction note to one responsibility
      --commit                           `propose`: append the items to the advisory backlog
      --json                             Print JSON instead of text
  -h, --help                             Print help
```

## mewkit budget

```text
Token and USD spend from the cost log

Usage: mewkit budget [OPTIONS] [SUBCOMMAND]

Arguments:
  [SUBCOMMAND]  `context` estimates a profile's load size; omitted reads the cost log

Options:
      --monthly                Aggregate by month instead of the last ten entries
      --session <SESSION>      Filter to the current session, or to a specific session id
      --day <DAY>              Filter to today, or to a specific YYYY-MM-DD
      --profile <PROFILE>      `context`: estimate one profile instead of all of them
      --fail-over <FAIL_OVER>  `context`: exit non-zero when a profile exceeds N tokens
      --json                   `context`: print the reports as JSON
  -h, --help                   Print help
```

## mewkit capabilities

```text
Explain, resolve and project the kit's capabilities

Usage: mewkit capabilities [OPTIONS] [SUBCOMMAND] [TARGET]

Arguments:
  [SUBCOMMAND]  `list` (default), `explain`, `resolve`, `view`, `bootstrap` or `projections`
  [TARGET]      `explain`: the capability id; `resolve`: the intent, when `--intent` is absent

Options:
      --json                 Print JSON instead of text
      --intent <INTENT>      `resolve`: the intent to resolve
      --provider <PROVIDER>  `resolve`: the host provider (default claude-code); `bootstrap`: the provider to render for
      --write                `bootstrap`: write the generated file instead of printing it
  -h, --help                 Print help
```
